The belief: by the time the constructor runs, the component is fully configured, inputs included, so it's the natural place to start work that depends on them.

That's how classes work everywhere else: the constructor receives what the object needs, and the object is ready when it returns. Developers coming from React expect the same, since a function component gets its props as an argument and can use them on its first line. Angular seems to confirm it, because services really are ready there.

works in a field initializer, and older code received services as constructor parameters. If the dependencies are there, why wouldn't the inputs be? The difference is where each one comes from. Services come from the injector, which Angular asks while it builds the instance. Inputs come from the parent's template, and Angular can only apply them to an instance that already exists.
